findings.issue: KMS key automatic rotation not enabled
findings.risk: Without automatic key rotation, the same cryptographic material is used indefinitely. If the key material is ever compromised, all data encrypted with it remains at risk with no periodic re-keying to limit the blast radius.
findings.remediation: Add 'enable_key_rotation = true' to the aws_kms_key.logs_key resource block to enable annual automatic rotation of the key material.

findings.issue: Excessively short KMS key deletion window
findings.risk: A deletion_window_in_days of 7 (the minimum) provides very little time to detect and cancel an accidental or malicious key deletion. If the key is deleted, any data encrypted with it becomes permanently unrecoverable.
findings.remediation: Increase 'deletion_window_in_days' to a value between 14 and 30 (e.g., 30) to provide a sufficient window to detect and cancel unintended key deletion requests.

findings.risk: Without an explicit key policy, the key falls back to the default AWS KMS key policy, which grants the AWS account root user full access. This may violate least-privilege principles and could allow any IAM principal with sufficient IAM permissions to use the key, broadening the potential attack surface.
findings.remediation: Add a 'policy' attribute to the aws_kms_key.logs_key resource containing an explicit key policy that restricts key administrators and key users to only the specific IAM roles/principals that require access, following the principle of least privilege.
